newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian president bans rallies after riots.
newsitem.headline: Armenian president bans rallies after riots.

text.p: Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan on Thursday banned all rallies and demonstrations after fierce clashes in the capital Yerevan between riot police and his political opponents.
Ter-Petrosyan, speaking on national television in the early hours, also vowed to punish all "provocateurs", blaming them for clashes outside the parliament building on Wednesday night.
"In accordance with the constitution I announce that all meetings, demonstrations and gatherings are forbidden without our permission," Ter-Petrosyan said.
"We will take other legal measures if needed. The provocateurs will be punished. We won't allow the very existence of Armenia...to be put into danger."
Police fired over the heads of a crowd which stormed the parliament grounds in Yerevan on Wednesday during protests about Ter-Petrosyan's victory in Sunday's presidential election.

The protesters say the vote was rigged to defeat former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan. They hurled bricks and police waded in with truncheons. At least seven protesters were hurt in the clashes. The opposition says one person was killed but the authorities deny it.
